tagline: The world's worst traffic — wrapped around a bay, a river and 7,000 islands.
summary: Metro Manila has some of the planet's most severe road congestion, on a metropolis built around Manila Bay, the Pasig River and Laguna Lake. The government is actively reviving urban water transport — the Pasig River Ferry now runs electric boats, and the planned MAPALLA (Manila Bay–Pasig River–Laguna Lake) system targets electric ferries by 2029. Beyond the capital, Cebu, Bohol and Palawan form a tailor-made archipelago network. This is Grab's largest pure-archipelago market.

use_cases.title: Manila Bay & Pasig fast lane
use_cases.body: Foiling shuttles across Manila Bay and along the Pasig — Makati/BGC to the bayfront and Cavite — turning gridlocked road trips into minutes on the water, alongside the city's own ferry revival.

use_cases.title: In-app water tier for Grab
use_cases.body: Bay and river crossings booked in the Grab app, door-to-door with a GrabCar each end — the water layer of the super-app in its largest archipelago market.

use_cases.body: Cebu ↔ Bohol ↔ Palawan (El Nido, Coron) island-hopping — Pioneer II for the capillaries, Quanta-LR for the long inter-island legs.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Manila Bay, Pasig and Cavite crossings are a handful of nautical miles — squarely all-electric. Cebu–Bohol-class hops sit inside 70 nm.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The long Visayas and Palawan inter-island legs (and Manila↔Palawan ambition) are Quanta-LR hybrid territory — no charging infrastructure across remote islands.

competitive_landscape: Urban water transport is government-led and reviving (Pasig River Ferry electric; MAPALLA). Inter-island is served by conventional fast-craft (OceanJet, 2GO) — slow and weather-exposed. No premium, on-demand, or foiling option exists; the government's own electrification push is a tailwind, not a competitor.
seasonality: Typhoon season (Jun–Nov) and the SW monsoon (habagat) drive rough conditions and ferry cancellations — exactly when foiling's smoother ride and Quanta-LR routing flexibility add the most value. Dry season (Dec–May) is peak tourism.
regulatory_note: Urban services align with DOTr / MMDA and the Pasig River Ferry framework; inter-island falls under MARINA. The government's electric-ferry mandate (MAPALLA) is an open door for a clean foiling standard.
signature_routes: Manila CBD ↔ Manila Bay ↔ Cavite (urban water-mobility)
